entry_conditions: Accept takeover within the full measured expanded transition, not only after a completed red release. The early observed state has red descending near the buffer around world [-0.181,0,0.02] m, but substantially above table height with closed measured total finger width around 0.0365 m and TCP/red association. For example demo10100:240 has red z=0.16279 m and demo10107:246 has red z=0.11536 m. Blue is still supported near its original positive-y region. At later entry red may already be supported with fingers opening or the empty TCP retreating, or blue may already be acquired in the incoming overlap. Use qpos[7:9] for measured aperture, qvel[9:18] fields for arm/finger motion as specified by the state schema, TCP pose[18:25], red pose[25:32], blue pose[32:39], goals[41:47] and two-state backward displacements. All poses are world metres and wxyz quaternions. Closed aperture plus proximity is evidence of association, not a contact sensor. Do not impose passive-red protection while it is still carried.
exit_conditions: A useful supported exit is blue actually resting near blue_goal [-0.35,-0.20,0.02] m, fingers closed on buffered red, and red rising with TCP association rather than the arm turning back toward blue. Demo10100:849 has red z=0.20283 m and blue z=0.02000 m. Demo10107:854 has red z=0.18144 m; its terminal state 855 has red z=0.19238 m, TCP z=0.19242 m and total finger width 0.03653 m while blue remains at z=0.02000 m. Preserve that red grip on transfer. Blue XY containment can occur during descent before release or retreat, so it alone is not the manipulation-readiness cue. These exit observations guide chaining; they do not add requirements to the supplied task completion contract.
overlap_role: The model learns the entire expanded slice with no preset schedule. Incoming overlap includes red descent, opening at the buffer, empty-hand upward retreat and blue approach/closure/lift. Red changes from active to passive and blue from passive to active, based on observed poses, aperture and backward motion. Outgoing overlap includes blue descent/placement, finger opening, retreat, return above the buffer, and red closure/lift. Blue then becomes passive and red active. At demo10100:275 red is supported and fingers total 0.07920 m but TCP is still at z=0.02304 m; by 320 TCP has retreated to z=0.30057 m. At 640 blue is supported with fingers opening, at 690 the open hand has retreated above it, and at 810 versus 820 red approach changes from open fingers to closed association. Graph role probabilities are learned causal cues, not fixed color assignments or a guarantee that motion is safe.
successor_readiness: Pass recent raw two-observation history with qpos/qvel, measured aperture, TCP pose, both object poses and world goals to finish_red. The successor needs blue genuinely supported at its achieved position and red/TCP grip and rising-motion evidence, not a high model passive score. It should continue closed-grip red lift/transport without reopening over the buffer or returning to blue. A supported-blue baseline can be reconstructed from recent measurements; this policy does not maintain or transmit a separate persistent baseline or phase state. Readiness may also be inferred earlier within the shared blue placement/retreat transition if the successor is deliberately chosen to finish that overlap.
failure_signatures: Previously supported red changes position/orientation during blue transit; blue leaves its goal during empty-hand retreat or red pickup; fingers close without subsequent red/TCP co-motion; red remains frozen when retrieval is intended; low predicted disturbance disagrees with observed movement; or the arm returns toward blue after red lift. Inspect measured object history and aperture rather than trusting stationary ensemble predictions. Full object pose, including z and orientation, matters: goal XY alone does not distinguish held from supported. These are diagnostic observations, not validated autonomous recovery rules.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy when red buffer descent/release is unfinished, blue remains active in pickup/transit/placement, or the observed open-hand retreat and red approach/closure/lift are still within demonstrated expanded support. Use two-state object and TCP displacement plus qvel and measured aperture to distinguish descent, open retreat and lift; do not rely on invocation age or original source indices. It can take over midway because all those motions are training actions and conditioning includes both objects and the actual robot state. Transfer to finish_red at the measured useful exit, or earlier within its shared overlap when the inference API elects it to finish the transition. Do not extend transfer_blue indefinitely into the untrained final red transport/placement. If observations depart materially from demonstrated sites or association is lost, reassess externally rather than interpreting a predicted passive role as safety. Task success remains red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal under the supplied rotated-containment and z-tolerance contract, without an added release/clearance/speed/hold predicate.
limitations: Boundary measurements are observed training support, not hard rejection thresholds or policy-performance evidence. Association/support are weakly inferred from geometry, aperture and recent displacement; no contact sensors, FK or IK are available. Only two causal observations are retained; dwell states and pre-command changes can be ambiguous and there is no persistent preservation baseline. Dynamics see successful routes only, and constant passive predictions can be wrong for unsafe actions. Clearance is only a differentiable TCP-point/oriented-cube training surrogate. The fixed interface supports no candidate ranking, so this package amortizes noninterference at training and does not claim online collision screening. Unseen collisions, pushed buffers and recovery are untested. No heuristic handoff cue redefines task success.
